We sell a wide range of products to adult consumers consisting of staple products with our iconic brands Zig-Zag® and Stoker’s®. lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Other receivables
lines.why: Owed by suppliers and others, not by customers (vendor non-trade receivables): operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: In 2025, approximately 75% of our net sales were derived from outsourced production operations and our capital expenditures have ranged between $4.6 million and $13.5 million per year over the previous three years.
In 2025, less than 10% of our revenues were generated outside of the U.S. We believe international sales represent a meaningful growth opportunity.
For the year ended December 31, 2025, we did not have any customers that accounted for 10% or more of our net sales for the year.

We had one customer that accounted for 10.2% of our net sales for the year ended December 31, 2024, and did not have any customers that accounted for 10% or more of our net sales for the year ended December 31, 2023.

Our tobacco products comprised approximately 62% of our total 2025 net sales and, while some of our sales volume declines have been offset by higher prices or by increased sales in other product categories, there can be no assurance that these price increases or increased sales can be sustained, especially in an environment of increased regulation, product characteristic restrictions, and taxation and changes in consumer spending habits.
In 2025, we had no customers that accounted for more than 10% of our net sales.
In 2024 we had one customer that accounted for more than 10% of our net sales and in 2023 we had no customers that accounted for more than 10% of our net sales.
For 2025, the Company did not have any customers that accounted for more than 10% of net sales.
There was one customer that accounted for more than 10% of net sales for 2024 and there were no customers that accounted for more than 10% of nets sales for 2023 .
The Company did not have any customers that accounted for more than 10% of net sales in 2025.
The Company had one customer that accounted for 10.2 % of net sales in 2024, of which 54 % was in the Stoker's product segment and 46 % was in the Zig-Zag products segment in 2024.
There were no customers that accounted for more than 10% of net sales in 2023.

“Risk Factors – We depend on a small number of key third-party suppliers and producers for our products.”
We depend on a small number of key third-party suppliers and producers for our products.
Our operations are largely dependent on a small number of key suppliers and producers to supply or manufacture our products pursuant to long-term contracts.
All of our loose-leaf tobacco products are manufactured for us by Swedish Match pursuant to a ten-year renewable agreement, which we entered into in 2008.
We rely on the performance by Swedish Match of its obligations under the agreement for the production of our loose-leaf tobacco products.

Further, a major fire, violent weather conditions or other disasters that affect us or any of our key suppliers or producers, including RTI or Swedish Match, as well as those of our other suppliers and vendors, could have a material adverse effect on our operations.
For example, we have witnessed a shift in consumer purchases from chewing tobacco to moist snuff due to its increased affordability.

In such an event, we may ultimately be forced to pursue and rely on local and more fragmented sales channels, which will have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

Under the terms of our contracts, we impose requirements on our major suppliers to maintain quality and comply with product specifications and requirements and on our third-party co-manufacturer to comply with all federal, state and local laws.
Our access to capital markets and the terms of such access depend on multiple factors including the condition of the capital markets, our operating performance and our credit ratings.

We increasingly rely on information technology systems for our internal communications, controls, reporting and relations with customers and suppliers and information technology is becoming a significantly important tool for our sales staff.
In engaging in these data-related activities, we rely on our own technology systems and software, and those of third-party vendors.

Typically, we rely on encryption and authentication technology licensed from third parties to enhance transmission security of confidential information in relation to financial and other sensitive information that we have on file.
Our success depends upon the continued contributions of our senior management.
We currently rely on trademark and other intellectual property rights to establish and protect our products, including the brand names and logos we own or license.

We rely on our technology infrastructure and information systems for our internal communications, controls, reporting and relations with customers and suppliers, to utilize our data, and to bill, collect, and make payments.

Activities include mandatory quarterly online training for all employees, technical security controls, enhanced data protection, the maintenance of backup and protective systems, policy review and implementation, the evaluation and retention of cybersecurity insurance, periodic assessments of third -party service providers to assess cyber preparedness of key vendors, and running simulated cybersecurity drills, including vulnerability scanning, penetration testing and disaster recovery exercises, throughout our organization.
We rely on long-standing relationships with high-quality, established manufacturers to provide the majority of our produced products.

In 2023, based on Docklight’s financial results, a decline in the revenue multiples for comparable public companies, and a significant change in Docklight’s business model, the Company deemed the investment in Docklight fully impaired resulting in a loss of $ 8.7 million which was recorded in investment (gain) loss for the year ended December 31, 2023.
